name: How does an accessible vanity differ from a standard bathroom vanity?

mainEntity.name: How does an accessible vanity differ from a standard bathroom vanity?

acceptedAnswer.text: An accessible vanity prioritizes knee clearance and reachability, whereas standard vanities use closed cabinetry that requires standing directly in front of the basin. Roll-under vanities feature open space beneath the sink, insulated pipe protection to prevent burns, and lever-operated or touchless faucets. The functional tradeoff is losing some traditional under-sink storage, which can be resolved by adding accessible recessed medicine cabinets, side linen towers, or open shelving within easy reach.
acceptedAnswer.description: Accessible vanities offer open knee space underneath for seated access and use lever faucets, whereas standard vanities feature closed cabinets that block seated use.
